title: feat(queue): standing issue↔queue coverage reconciliation (#7016)
body: Closes #7016 ## Problem Nothing reconciles the open-issue set against fleet-queue coverage. Issues enter the queue only when a creator-class lane files them (file + enqueue in the same pass); anything filed another way — a work lane filing a blocker mid-task, an audit lane, by hand, or predating the queue (epics) — silently never gets a queue item, so no lane ever dispositions it. The 2026-11-07 reconciliation found 23 such issues across the four repos; that day's import was a one-off. ## What this adds **Broker — read-only `POST /coverage`.** Given the open-issue set the caller just enumerated, it answers per issue whether a **live** task (`queued`/`claimed`/`parked`/`blocked`) holds its repo-health dedupe key in the named queue. Per Drew's doctrine (2026-11-07): a `done` task is **not** coverage (done means triage or a landed slice, not a resolved issue), and neither is a task in a `*-shadow` queue. It never writes tasks or events. **`scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/`** — the scheduled job: - enumerates open issues with `gh api --paginate` (PRs filtered out; a partial page would read as coverage that does not exist), - asks the broker for the diff, - with `--import`, enqueues a triage packet per uncovered issue **through the sanctioned CLI path**, dedupe-keyed `repo-health:v1:triage::issue:` so re-runs are idempotent by construction, - **observe-only by default**, matching the sweeper revalidator's two-step rollout, - a fetch or broker failure exits **3** and names the repo in an ERRORS section — it never reports as "0 uncovered". **systemd units** (hourly at :41, `Persistent`) + a row in `doc/fleet-schedule-registry.md` per the same-pass rule. **`AGENTS.md`**: the file-and-enqueue rule for issues filed outside a creator run. ## Acceptance - [x] A scheduled reconciliation exists — `queue-coverage-reconcile.timer`, hourly, persistent. - [ ] Its first run reports 0 uncovered — **pending deployment**: the units are repo-shipped but not installed, and the running broker does not yet serve `/coverage` (it needs a rebuild + restart). Verified end-to-end today: GitHub enumeration succeeds, the broker answers `unknown command /coverage`, and the script exits 3 with the repo named rather than reporting a false zero. Once the broker is redeployed the timer's first cycle produces the real number in `~/.local/state/queue-reconcile/latest.md`. - [x] The file-and-enqueue rule is written into `AGENTS.md`. ## Unrelated fix included `validate.rs`: `FLEET_REPOS` is declared `[&str; 10]` but holds **9** entries, so the `fleet-queue` lib test target does not compile at `main` with `--all-features`. CI does not build this crate, so the defect was invisible there. One-character fix; it blocks the test target this change needs. ## Tests ``` cargo test -p fleet-queue --all-features 100 passed (lib), 2 passed (integration), 0 failed python3 -I scripts/fleet/queue-reconcile/test_check_coverage.py 6 passed ``` New coverage: 4 parser cases + 2 `proptest` properties on the dedupe-key parser (canonical keys round-trip for every class and dispatch suffix; another repo's key never matches), and 6 offline script tests (observe imports nothing, import enqueues exactly the uncovered set, full coverage imports nothing, fetch failure is an error not a zero, packet shape, report written). The packet the script builds validates against the live broker: `repo-queue validate` → `packet valid (repo-task/v1)`. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.
